Confirm your weekly hours, shift schedule, and whether weekend or night work is required.

4. Contract & Benefits
Check your holiday entitlement, pension, bonuses, and any additional company benefits.

Will you have opportunities to learn new skills and progress within the company?

We have observed a recurring pattern where highly qualified African professionals miss out on global opportunities not because they lack the skill but because they lack the proof. In a digital economy, five years of experience is a claim, while a public project is evidence.

When a founder or a project manager is hiring a Virtual Assistant or a Digital Marketer from across the continent, they are often looking for one thing: Can this person do the work right now?

A resume might say you understand project management. A shared Trello board or a case study of a past project shows how you actually think and organize. This shift from credentials to competence is why many self-taught individuals are outcompeting degree holders for remote roles.

One practical way to adapt is to stop only updating your resume and start building a Proof of Work folder. This could be a collection of published articles, a screen recording of a technical process you mastered, or a folder of design assets.

In Ruli, Rwanda, miners haul 30-70 kg bags of tungsten out of tunnels for 10 to 50 cents a bag. 
Their entire work history lives as tick marks in a paper booklet.

Across Africa's informal economy, workers build skills and prove themselves for years. Then a job ends, and the record of it vanishes. 
That missing history shapes access to finance, insurance, and the next job.

Fixa is fixing this. 

They started as a labour contracting platform in Rwanda, supplying workers into construction. But every worker onboarded, every shift completed, every payroll run was quietly creating something that barely exists across the continent: verified employment data. 

So far, more than 20,000 digital employment identities, over 1 million shifts, and US$6 million in wages processed. Over 95% of their workers accessed earned wages for the first time in their lives.

What made us confident?
Plenty of platforms try to sell financial services into the informal economy before they've earned trust or built data. 
Fixa works the opposite way. Solve a real operational problem for employers first, build trusted employment records as a by-product, then use those records to unlock better services for workers.

Reposting this because the upcoming changes to unfair dismissal protection will make one thing increasingly important: what happens in the first six months of employment. 🙌🏼

A situation I have seen more than once:

“We need to dismiss them.”

Okay. What happened?

“Well… they’ve been struggling for a while.”

How long is “a while”?

“About four months.”

Excellent. And what feedback have they had?

“Not much.”

Right.

And what was discussed at probation?

“Nothing formal.”

At this point, HR is expected to perform an employment law exorcism and fix six months of poor management in one meeting.

The better approach starts much earlier.

Before the employee starts:
→ Is the role and expectation clear?

During onboarding:
→ Are they actually being set up to succeed?

At probation:
→ Is there an honest assessment of performance and fit?

When concerns arise:
→ Are they being addressed early, clearly and consistently?

That is where my experience across Talent Acquisition and HR has been particularly valuable.

The recruitment decision is only the beginning. If the process from “we want to hire them” to “we need to dismiss them” is disconnected, the problem is usually not created at the end.

It has been quietly accumulating for months.

The upcoming changes make getting that process right even more important.

And, ideally, mean fewer meetings beginning with: “We need to get rid of them” and ending with everyone looking at HR as though we have a magic wand. (Newsflash, we don’t) 👀

A key part of our consulting work at Hito HR involves helping organisations attract and hire the right people.

While recruitment may appear straightforward, the reality is often far more complex, particularly for organisations operating within tight budgets.

One lesson has become increasingly clear over the years: Talent is not cheap. Neither is hiring the wrong person.
